# ComfyUI for coding agents

Use this fork to generate and edit images, video, audio, and text with ComfyUI
workflows from a terminal or Python application. It supplies the `comfyui` CLI,
an embedded client, custom-node Python packages, model discovery, and supported
multi-GPU execution. Deliver the requested artifacts and the settings needed to
reproduce them. Do not substitute a workflow description for running the task.

Read the applicable guide in full before relying on its instructions. Vendor
snapshots retain their source material and attribution; they may describe hosted
models or APIs, not installed ComfyUI nodes. Use their prompting guidance with
the actual model and workflow you selected.

## Establish the environment

Use an existing compatible environment and workspace when available. Inspect the
installed `comfyui`, Python, Torch backend, accelerator, and available model files.
Run `comfyui env` for an environment report. Do not delete or recreate an existing
environment merely because its Python version differs from an example. The
package metadata allows Python >=3.10; dependencies and extension wheels impose
additional constraints. The compatibility guide describes configured CI stacks.

For a new Linux/macOS workspace with uv installed:

```console
mkdir -p ComfyUI_Workspace
cd ComfyUI_Workspace
uv venv --python 3.12
uv pip install --torch-backend=auto --extra-index-url https://nodes.appmana.com/simple/ comfyui
source .venv/bin/activate
comfyui env
```

For Windows activation and AMD/Intel-specific installation, use the installation
guide. Keep an existing accelerator stack pinned when adding packages. Extensions
such as SageAttention, FlashAttention, Triton, or Nunchaku are optional and require
matching hardware and wheels; do not install them indiscriminately. A virtual
environment contains platform-specific binaries and is not a portable bundle for
an arbitrary host.

Reuse models with `--cwd`, `--extra-model-paths-config`, or
`--add-model-folder-path checkpoints=/path/to/checkpoints`. For gated models,
accept the publisher's terms and use `hf auth login` or `HF_TOKEN`. Keep credentials
out of generated examples and reports.

## Choose and inspect a workflow

```console
comfyui workflows list
comfyui run-workflow workflow.json --help
comfyui workflows params workflow.json --all
comfyui models --help
```

Start with a template or a known complete workflow for the requested model family.
The runner accepts template names, UI/API JSON files, supported URIs, and stdin.
Read author notes and inspect the discovered parameters before changing nodes.
UI graphs are converted automatically; API graphs use node IDs with `class_type`
and `inputs`. A loader node alone is not an executable image-generation workflow:
include conditioning, sampling, decoding, and an output node as appropriate.

Match the checkpoint/diffusion model, text encoder, VAE, LoRA, and conditioning
nodes. For example, an SDXL LoRA belongs with an SDXL-compatible model, and a
FLUX.1 LoRA is not interchangeable with FLUX.2 Klein. A downloaded file or registry
search result is not evidence that a model architecture is supported locally.

## Prepare and run

```console
comfyui run-workflow workflow.json --dry-run
comfyui run-workflow workflow.json --all --prompt "a small observatory in a snowy forest" --seed 42
```

`--dry-run` reports planned packages and model downloads without inference; remote
metadata access can still occur. `--all` installs missing node packages and
resolvable models. Honor the user's permissions for downloads and installations.
Unknown nodes or missing filenames may require manual resolution. The facade
can build missing registry packages locally, but cannot guarantee compatibility
with every third-party repository.

Override only inputs supported by the workflow. Common options include `--prompt`,
`--negative-prompt`, `--seed`, `--steps`, `--width`, `--height`, `--cfg`, `--image`,
`--video`, and `--audio`. Workflow help also exposes discovered flags. For an exact
API node input, use `--set '6.inputs.text=a lighthouse at dusk'`, replacing `6`
with the actual node ID. `--quantity` repeats jobs; `--batch-size` changes latent
batch inputs and can require more memory.

JSON results go to stdout and normal logs to stderr:

```console
comfyui run-workflow workflow.json --seed 42 > result.jsonl
```

Read the returned output fields to locate artifacts. Check that the files exist
and inspect the actual image, video, or audio before claiming success. Preserve
the workflow, seed, model revisions, and overrides alongside the result. Do not
infer success merely from a zero exit code or a preview image.

## Prompt and iterate

State the subject, action, composition, environment, lighting, material, and visual
style in terms the selected model understands. Use the corresponding vendor guide
for model-specific syntax. Do not automatically apply SD-style weighted tags or
negative prompts to models trained for natural language instructions.

For image editing, identify what must change and what must remain: subject identity,
pose, layout, palette, or background. Supply the reference through the workflow's
image inputs and check how multiple reference slots are assigned. For video,
describe temporal action and camera motion, and use the workflow's supported
duration, frame count, and resolution. An image-to-video workflow needs its actual
image input; a text prompt does not replace it.

For pixel art, specify subject readability, silhouette, palette, and intended
pixel scale. Inspect edges and the final displayed size. A prompt alone does not
guarantee a consistent pixel grid; use a suitable workflow or post-processing when
the user requires exact pixel dimensions or lattice alignment.

Generate a small initial sample, inspect it against the request, and vary one
meaningful factor at a time. Keep seeds fixed when comparing prompt/settings
changes. Do not report invented performance measurements or guaranteed quality.

## Reuse execution state for batches

Pass several files to one runner invocation, or retain a single `Comfy` instance:

```python
import asyncio
import json
from pathlib import Path
from comfy.client.embedded_comfy_client import Comfy


async def main():
    async with Comfy() as client:
        for path in sorted(Path("workflows").glob("*.json")):
            workflow = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            outputs = await client.queue_prompt(workflow)
            print(path.name, outputs)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

This allows eligible weights and execution caches to remain resident. Memory
pressure, model changes, or configuration changes can still trigger unloading or
worker replacement. The embedded client defaults to a thread executor; incompatible
global configuration can require a subprocess. Progress streaming currently works
on the thread path, not across the process-executor boundary. See the embedded
guide for lifetime and configuration details.

## Memory and multiple GPUs

Begin with hardware-aware defaults. Use `--reserve-vram` when sharing the GPU with
other applications. `--novram` disables DynamicVRAM and smart memory management;
it is an explicit fallback, not a prerequisite for every low-memory device.
Compilation adds warmup and may not help a short run. Quantized storage does not
guarantee a faster compute kernel or compatibility with every parallel mode.

Tensor parallelism splits supported model operations; pipeline parallelism mainly
increases capacity; sequence parallelism splits supported attention workloads.
Use the performance guide's family and hardware restrictions. Automatic selection
does not promise a speedup. Queue workers increase independent-job throughput and
require separate deployment/storage configuration.

## Finish with evidence

Return the generated artifact paths or links and a concise explanation of what
was produced. Include the final workflow and material settings needed to reproduce
it. If execution failed, report the actual error and the missing dependency,
model, access permission, or capacity constraint; do not present an unexecuted
workflow as a completed generation.

## Practical recipes

### Restyle a portrait

Find an image-edit workflow for a locally supported model. Save it as
`portrait-edit.json` and inspect its inputs:

```console
comfyui workflows search "portrait image edit" --limit 5 --json
comfyui run-workflow portrait-edit.json --help
comfyui run-workflow portrait-edit.json --dry-run
comfyui run-workflow portrait-edit.json --all --image portrait.png --prompt "Restyle this portrait as a Renaissance oil painting with soft window light and a muted earth palette. Preserve the person's identity, pose, and framing." --seed 42
```

The search is a discovery step; obtain the selected workflow before the commands
that reference the local file. Inspect the result for identity and composition
preservation. If using a style LoRA, search with `comfyui models search --help`
and choose one that matches the edit model's architecture before adding it.

### Animate a still

Choose an image-to-video workflow that fits the available memory, save it as
`animate.json`, and inspect its frame-count, resolution, and motion controls:

```console
comfyui run-workflow animate.json --help
comfyui run-workflow animate.json --all --image dancer.png --prompt "The dancer takes two graceful steps and turns, fabric following the motion. Locked camera, consistent lighting, stable background." --seed 42
```

Set duration through the actual workflow's exposed controls rather than inventing
a universal duration flag. Review the resulting clip for temporal consistency,
motion, and the requested length; a single preview frame is insufficient.

### Reproduce a community workflow

Use `comfyui workflows search` to obtain a workflow URI, then pass that exact URI
to `comfyui run-workflow URI --help`. Read the author notes, inspect model and node
requirements with `--dry-run`, then run with `--all` when installation is authorized.
A Civitai model-version URI identifies an asset and is not necessarily a workflow;
use model assets with compatible loader or LoRA options. Preserve the original
workflow and record changes to inputs, seeds, or model versions when reproducing it.
